@@ -157,7 +157,7 @@ The composer owns artifact detail selection, anchoring, dismissal and model life

The panel and its state-list, Autopilot and Activities widgets render presentation-ready data and invoke its commands. They do not acquire provider details or inspect provider snapshots. List and action identities are provider-qualified; selected tabs, expanded cards and prepared policies belong to artifact-scoped view state, separately from durable automation settings. Closing details releases live subscriptions without changing recorded request-card snapshots.

-Chats may expose server-published live canvases through an observable provider-neutral collection when the owning provider permits canvas presentation for that session. Each chat discovers membership from its advertised canvas channel references; each subscribed channel supplies presentation metadata and an optional live HTTP(S) source. Unknown membership is distinct from an authoritative empty collection, and pending canvas state retains its resource without a source. Registered canvas-definition listings use the same distinction: `undefined` means the provider registry is unsettled and consumers retain the last authoritative listing, while an empty array authoritatively clears it. A provider that returns `undefined` must publish another canvas change after the registry settles so consumers request the authoritative snapshot. The local Agent Host provider enables presentation only for durable Copilot sessions, while ephemeral and remote sessions expose no canvas capability. Canvas execution and presentation continue to follow the existing canvas enablement setting. Session and chat switches suspend presentation while retaining the live browser model, so returning reattaches the same page and browser-side state. Closing presentation dismisses that canvas lifetime without invoking provider operations; archive, deletion, authoritative membership removal, or source replacement releases its browser model. Closing the canvas itself is a separate user operation that names the canvas by its channel. The Agents Window routes it through `ISessionsManagementService` to the owning provider, and the Editor Window through the chat's canvas context; either way the host ends that live canvas and notifies its canvas provider, and the resulting authoritative membership removal releases the presentation. Metadata and source updates do not reopen a dismissed canvas; a later successful model request to open that instance explicitly permits revealing the existing lifetime again. Open-request identity is derived from the owning chat's tool state and is client-only presentation metadata, not a canvas-channel revision. Canvas membership, sources, and browser models are not persisted across restarts. The workbench owns the shared canvas editor, presentation lifecycle, and retained browser models; the Agents Window supplies its active-session/active-chat context, editor working sets, and layout policy, while the Editor Window permits exact owners represented by visible chat widgets.

+Chats may expose server-published live canvases through an observable provider-neutral collection when the owning provider permits canvas presentation for that session. Each chat discovers membership from its advertised canvas channel references; each subscribed channel supplies presentation metadata and an optional live HTTP(S) source. Unknown membership is distinct from an authoritative empty collection, and pending canvas state retains its resource without a source. Registered canvas-definition listings use the same distinction: `undefined` means the provider registry is unsettled and consumers retain the last authoritative listing, while an empty array authoritatively clears it. A provider that returns `undefined` must publish another canvas change after the registry settles so consumers request the authoritative snapshot. Agent Host providers enable presentation only for durable Copilot sessions; ephemeral sessions expose no canvas capability. Remote sessions expose it only while browser remote proxying is enabled, unless their host is known not to proxy browser connections, so a temporary disconnect keeps their canvases. The Agents Window routes it through `ISessionsManagementService` to the owning provider, and the Editor Window through the chat's canvas context; either way the host ends that live canvas and notifies its canvas provider, and the resulting authoritative membership removal releases the presentation. Metadata and source updates do not reopen a dismissed canvas; a later successful model request to open that instance explicitly permits revealing the existing lifetime again. Open-request identity is derived from the owning chat's tool state and is client-only presentation metadata, not a canvas-channel revision.
